Commentary.Commentary: Right then! The players and the umpires walk out once again and take the field to start the run chase. USA Women Under-19 need 98 runs in 120 deliveries. It's the pair of Disha Dhingra and Chetna Reddy Pagydyala to open the batting for the USA Women Under-19. Louisa Kotkamp has the new ball in hand for New Zealand Women Under-19. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

98 runs required for the USA Women Under-19 to win the game and climb onto the number 2 spot on the table. Will the USA manage the same batting performance they have shown previously in the tournament? Or will the New Zealand Women Under-19 bowlers steal the show and take their team to a second win? Let's find out in the Run Chase starting very soon. Stay tuned!

Ritu Singh from the USA Women Under-19 is up for a quick chat after taking a stellar 5-fer. She says that the wicket was a bit stickier in Johor. Mentions that she does not have much experience on turf wickets so these conditions are pretty new to her. She thanks her skipper and the coach for talking to her about sticking to her plans. On being asked about her favorite wicket, she says that the first wicket was a crucial one as they were a bit under pressure early on. Tells that her plan was to keep it fuller and slower to deceive the batters in the flight.

The New Zealand Women Under-19 started off well with 32 runs inside the first 5 overs with the new ball. Both the openers went out and started hitting boundaries and the batting looked really easy. Ritu Singh was introduced in the fifth over of the innings and she took the first wicket in her first over itself. New Zealand Women Under-19 then lost the next 4 wickets inside 11 runs and were thrown off the game by the USA Women Under-19 bowlers. The lower order managed a few partnerships but Ritu Singh and her bowling partners kept taking the wickets and ended the innings for 97 runs.

New Zealand Women Under-19 are bowled out for 97 runs with 1 ball remaining in the first innings. Ritu Singh walks away with a wide smile on her face and a FIVE WICKET HAUL for the USA Women Under-19. With 98 runs to chase and the batting order of USA Women Under-19 being in the form that they are in, this looks like an easy chase. Still, cricket is always a game of uncertainties.

OUT! TAKEN! Ritu Singh wraps New Zealand's innings with a spectacular 5-wicket haul. All the USA players converge and acknowledge her in unison! Ritu Singh keeps providing more flight on the ball and lands it outside off, on a fullish length, Sophie Court spreads across and looks to work it in the off side. She gets lured into the flight and goes through the shot very early. Hence a healthy leading edge is found and the ball lobs up in the air. It dips towards the fielder stationed at point. Maahi Madhavan there takes a safe catch. New Zealand Women Under-19 are bundled up on 97 with a ball to spare.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all done with the pre-match formalities, and it is now time for the action to commence at the YSD-UKM Cricket Oval, Bangi. The weather is clear with a few scattered clouds, but nothing as threatening which is a pleasing thing. The umpires and players are out in the middle. We have got a fair bit of crowd and supporters at the venue for both sides. Now then, the players of USA Women Under-19 form a team huddle before spreading out in the field. Out walk the opening pair of Emma McLeod and Kate Irwin for New Zealand Women Under-19. Maahi Madhavan has the new ball and is all in readiness to kickoff the proceedings. Off we go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of this game, but before that, the two sets of players stride out with the match officials for their respective national anthems. It will New Zealand's first, followed by the national anthem of the USA.

PITCH REPORT - Stacy-Ann King is inspecting the pitch. She informs about the dimensions of the ground and says it is a 68-meter straight hit and the squares are 57 meters and 56 meters respectively. Mentions that 12 matches have been played so far on this track and 72 wickets have fallen, so bowlers will enjoy bowling on this surface. Observes that there's a bit of moisture on the surface and it is a bit tacky due to some heavy rain around in the past few days. Also reckons that if the batters apply well, they can score good runs.

The skipper of New Zealand Women Under-19, Tash Wakelin says that they were looking to bat first and are happy with the toss. She further adds that their previous game was a good one for them and they walk in with confidence in this one. With just one win on the board, it is very tough to recollect the will to fight but the team and the management have been on their toes and are looking for this win, says Tash in the end.

The captain of USA Women Under-19, Anika Kolan says that the pitch has a bit of moisture and reckons it will play better later on. Mentions that they are excited about how they perform in this game. Adds they took a lot of positives from the previous games and are constantly learning. Ends by saying she expects them to put in some strong performance this time around. Informs one change.

New Zealand's journey through the tournament has been less than stellar, concluding third in Group C. Placed in a challenging group alongside South Africa, Nigeria, and Samoa, the Kiwi side experienced two losses, with their defeat against Nigeria being particularly unexpected. Their solitary victory came against Samoa in a one-sided encounter. Weather conditions played a significant role, with rain interrupting and reducing all matches played so far. Despite the team's struggles, individual performances have been noteworthy. Eve Wolland has emerged as their primary batting talent, complemented by Emma McLeod's contributions in the middle order. On the bowling front, skipper Tash Wakelin has led the wicket-taking efforts, which have been supported effectively by Rishika Jaswal and Sophie Court. The United States Women Under-19 team has carved out an intriguing path in the tournament, securing second place in Group B with a performance that has captured attention. Their group stage journey has experienced the full spectrum of match outcomes - a victory, a defeat, and a washout. Their notable triumph came against Ireland, while they encountered a comprehensive defeat at the hands of tournament favorites England. Under the leadership of Anika Kolan, the team has demonstrated commendable batting depth and resilience. The opening partnership of Disha Dhingra and Chetna Reddy Pagydyala has shown promising signs, particularly in their match against Ireland. Captain Kolan herself has complemented her leadership with meaningful batting contributions, adding stability to the team's middle order. The bowling department has not been left behind, with Isani Vaghela emerging as a standout performer, spearheading the attack impressively. The team's balanced approach and versatility suggest they will pose a significant challenge in the Super Sixes stage. But can they compete strongly against a much heavier side in New Zealand?
